BULLETIN No: 123/26 Dated: 14th October-2026 Time: 11:00 hours (PST)

RIVERS AT A GLANCE

FLOOD SEVERITY SCALE

RAINFALL FORECAST — NEXT 24 & 48 HOURS

RIVERS SITUATION AND QUALITATIVE FLOOD FORECAST

I.      METEOROLOGICAL FEATURES

  • Yesterday's trough of westerly wave over the northern parts of the country persists.

II.     METEOROLOGICAL OUTLOOK              

  • Isolated to Scattered rain-wind/thunderstorm is expected over the upper catchments of all the major rivers, Islamabad, Kashmir, Gilgit Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Upper Punjab and Balochistan.

III.    HYDROLOGICAL SITUATION at 0600 PST

  • All major rivers are flowing in their normal flows at all gauging stations. 

IV.    HYDROLOGICAL OUTLOOK

  • Flows in all major rivers are expected to remain within the normal flow range at their respective rim stations. However, flows may rise slightly in the tributaries of Kabul river.
 

V.     WEATHER FORECAST FOR 24-HOUR

  • Scattered rain-wind/thunderstorm with isolated heavy falls is expected over the upper catchments of all the major rivers, Islamabad, Kashmir, Gilgit Baltistan,

    Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Abbottabad, Bajaur, Batagram, Buner, Chitral, Haripur, Kohistan, Dir, Malakand, Mansehra, Mardan, Mohmand, Shangla, Swabi, Swat and Tor Ghar.

    Punjab: Gujrat, Narowal, Rawalpindi and Sialkot.

  • Isolated rain-wind/thunderstorm is expected over

    Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Bannu, Charsadda, Hangu, Karak, Khyber, Kohat, Kurram, Waziristan, Nowshera, Orakzai and Peshawar.

    Punjab: Attock, Chakwal, Chiniot, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Jhelum, Kasur, Khushab, Lahore, Mandi Bahauddin, Mianwali, Nankana Sahib, Okara, Pakpattan, Sargodha, Sheikhupura and Toba Tek Singh.

VI.    WEATHER OUTLOOK FOR NEXT 48-HOURS   

  • Mainly dry weather is expected over the most parts of the country, however, Isolated rain-wind/thunderstorm is expected over the upper catchments of river  Chenab and Jhelum, Kashmir, Gilgit Baltistan,

    Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Batagram, Kohistan and Mansehra.

    Punjab: Gujranwala, Gujrat, Lahore, Narowal, Sheikhupura and Sialkot.

     

WEEKLY SIGNIFICANT OUTLOOK 

(15th  October, 2026 to 20th October, 2026)

I.      RAINFALL OUTLOOK

  • Mainly dry weather is expected over the most parts of the country.

II.     FLOOD OUTLOOK

  • Flows are expected to remain normal at all rim stations of all the major rivers during the period.

3. WEATHER/RAINFALL FORECAST FOR NEXT 24-HRS

4. QUANTITATIVE FLOOD FORECAST OF GAUGING STATIONS (IN THOUSANDS OF CUSECS)

Spatial: Isolated=20 to 30% of area | Scattered=31 to 50% of area | Fairly Widespread=51 to 75% of area | Widespread=76 to 100% of area, R= Rising, F=Falling

Intensity (mm/24 hours): Light ≤ 10, Moderate =10.1 – 30, Heavy=30.1 – 70, Very Heavy=70.1 - 150, Extremely Heavy > 150

Note: Concerned Departments may contact FFD, Lahore for rectification up-dation (if any)

5. HOW CLOSE IS EACH RIVER TO ITS LIMIT?

Sidhnai is the closest to flooding at 13.0 — 17.0 below its low flood level (30.0). Each bar is one station’s own flood levels across its maximum capacity; the solid run is the flow so far, the pale run is the room still left.

All figures in thousands of cusecs. Full bar = maximum (design) capacity. Solid colour is the flow reached so far and the pale wash beside it is the room still left; the dark line between them is the current reading, printed beneath it. Thin white lines are that station’s flood levels with their thresholds beneath, so the same colour can begin at a different point on every bar. Each band is named inside itself — initialled (BL, L, M, H, VH, EH) where the band is too narrow for the words, and left blank where it is too narrow for those. Stations without a design capacity are not shown.
